text:
maria: Quick heads-up — found a weird conversion bug from HF chat_template -> Redwood prompt that caused a quality regression in our bring-up evals. Repro snippet:

maria: HF chat_template (simplified):
```json
{"role": "system", "content": "{% if system_prompt %}{{ system_prompt }}{% endif %}"},
{"role": "user", "content": "{{ user_input }}"}
```

maria: When system_prompt is empty, rendered messages array becomes `[ {role: \"system\", content: \"\"}, {role: \"user\", content: \"hi\"} ]` and our converter flattens to a single prompt string that drops the system role instead of preserving an empty system message. Outputs change a lot.

kevin: Oof. Do you have the eval numbers? tokenizer/conf maybe?

maria: Eval run 2026-03-12-21: qa_f1 dropped 92.1 -> 86.0 on our onboarding suite after conversion for the new quantized variant. Tokenizer mismatch looked unlikely — tokens line up — it's specifically role/ordering in the prompt.

sara: Sounds like role-attrition. Our HF->Redwood converter currently does: join(messages, "\n\n") and that loses per-message role metadata when content is empty. Example transform (pseudo):
```py
# bad: flattens and loses empty system role
rendered = "\n\n".join(m['content'] for m in hf_chat_template)
redwood_prompt = render(rendered)
```
This means assistant/system signals get merged into user if the first content is empty.

alex: Quick workaround we used in a local run — inject a tiny nonprinting sentinel into system when empty, then strip it at runtime. e.g. set system content to "<|sys_sentinel|>" when empty and change converter to replace that with "" after preserving role metadata. Example patch:
```py
for m in hf_messages:
    if m['role'] == 'system' and not m['content'].strip():
        m['content'] = '<|SYS|>'
# later: when assembling for model, include role markers then drop sentinel
```
This preserved the role boundary and fixed the regression locally.

maria: Confirmed — with sentinel injection the qa_f1 recovered to 91.8 (almost baseline). Not perfect but huge improvement.

kevin: Nice. Long-term fix is to keep the messages as structured array through the conversion (preserve role field) instead of joining blindly. The runtime already supports role-aware assembly; we should use that path.

sara: I'll open a PR that makes convert_chat_template output an explicit array of {role, text} into the RW prompt builder API instead of a joined string. Add a unit test for empty-system, conditional blocks and nested jinja (weirdly some templates use `{% if system %}{{ system }}{% endif %}` vs `{{ system|default('') }}`).

alex: I'll review. Also let's add an integration test in eval harness so we catch regressions: run new-model bring-up on both raw and converted prompt and diff key metrics automatically.

maria: One more note — quantized/8-bit models are more sensitive to these formatting shifts (kv-cache alignment and initial token biases), so small role bleed can amplify. Callout in PR description please.

eval-bot: Ran quick smoke eval on 1835123456-workaround: qa_f1=91.8, latency +2ms, tokens identical. Full eval queued: https://ci.redwood-inference/internal/evals/7789

sara: linking issue for tracking + design discussion: https://github.com/redwood-inference/platform/issues/1234

maria: thanks all. i'll keep the sentinel workaround on the staging branch until PR merges. :thumbsup:

kevin: small follow-up: add a comment in the converter explaining why sentinel is needed (references to this thread + issue). saves future confusion.

alex: agreed. i'll add it in review. :ok_hand:
